_doc: MN-11 status-aware lines. b=band of the SUBJECT's status as the speaker reads it, s=situation (greet|gossip|gate|companion), c=culture or *, sp=species or *. Original text.

lines.t: Keep walking. Nobody here owes you a bench.
I have seen kinder faces on a gallows.
Mind the dog, not the stranger. You smell of trouble.
Your name came ahead of you, and it came limping.
We do not serve your sort. Try the road.
They say the one with the beast was run out of two towns.
Heard that one is wanted. Heard worse, too.
Not a coin, not a word, not a step.
That thing eats more than my whole house.
A walker with no name walks alone.
Unclean. Turn back.
Be cleansed or be elsewhere.
Morning. Do not linger by the stalls, friend.
Lord's own hound? Mind your feet.
Do I know you? No. Good.
Wipe your boots, and take that lead up short.
You are new here. New folk pay first.
Someone said a traveller came through with a tamed wolf. Might be you.
They say you spoke it a name. What is it like, to be answered?
Papers, then the fee, then the lead. In that order.
Registry is at the red door. Collar is three marks, tags are free.
That one stays outside. Camp by the hitching rail.
Fine beast. Keep it where I can see it.
Name-bearer. The ash-poles do not know your face yet.
The Throne counts souls. Yours is on loan to that creature.
Fair day to you. Mind the cart ruts by the well.
Traveller. Bread is fresh if you have coin.
You have the look of someone who pays on time.
Evening, neighbour. Quiet streets tonight.
Stable's out back if you need a stall.
The knight with the ogre? He pays for his own broken doors.
Heard she named a whole pack. Hair went white that night.
They say the goblin does the books better than my nephew. Do not tell him.
Fee is two marks a head. Smile for the clerk.
Your goblin did my accounts better than my nephew. Do not tell him.
Does the lizard bite? No? Then it can have the bench.
Kobold miners are welcome at the shaft head.
Wolf of the hills! Hunters will stand it a round.
Beasts are kin-spirits. Walk with it kindly.
Good day to you. The council spoke well of your last favour.
Come by the hall; there is a stool kept for you.
Your name carries in the market. Keep it clean.
Ah, you. The baker saved the good loaf.
Folk speak well of you in the guild row.
Her wolf spoke, you know. Cold. Rain. Stay. Three words and the priest was fetched.
He keeps his word to the beast and to the bank. Rare.
They say the charter held in two towns already.
Sponsored? Then pass, and take the hitching rail on the house.
Pass, name-bearer. The ash-poles know your face.
A named beast. Is it papers it carries, or only a tooth for show?
A baker leaves bread at the gate for your ogre now. Do not ask.
The Throne forgives much for a seal and a tithe.
My lord, my lady. The hall is yours.
Rare to see a house keep such company with such grace.
The steward will clear the east stable for your companions.
Your charter is read aloud at our gate. Pass freely.
They say the Crown listens when you ask.
The envoy who walks with the lizardfolk argues better than my own chancellor.
It was your word that opened the ban for a season. We remember.
No fee for the charter-holder. Bows all round.
Come back with a charter and I will hear you.
The elders will hear you, name-bearer. Sit.
A beast at table is a beast with manners. Pour it water.
Hail. The lamps are lit for you tonight.
History sits with you at this table.
You need no papers. You are the paper.
Children chalk your sigil on the lintels.
Even the Throne's clerks lower their eyes.
They sing of the name-giver in three kingdoms, and each version has a different dragon.
They say she named a dragon. She says it was a lizard. They say you cannot tell the difference at that size.
Open the main gate! The whole company, and no questions.
Let the beast lead. It has earned the first step.
The ash-poles bow to you, first of the name-bearers.
I heard he named a demon and it named him back.
Heard she was named by the monster. Could be true.
Someone swears it was a dragon. A big one. At the pass.
